SPECIFICATION FOR STATIC PROTECTIVE RELAYS 0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Sandard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 28 October 1977, after the draft finalized by the Relays Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrbtechnical Division Council. 0.2 The requirements for the electrical relays used for power system protection are covered in IS : 3231-1965*. This standard has been prepared with a view to cover the additional requirements for static relays than those covered in IS : 3231-1965*. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from IEC Pub 255-4 Single input energizing quantity measuring relays with E!ectrotechnical dependent specified time, issued by the International Commission. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing with the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance IS : 2-1960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value shouId be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard equipment.
2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions in addition and IS : 1885 (Part X)-1968$ to those given in IS : 1885 (Part 1X)-1966: shall apply. 2.1 Static Protective response is developed mechanical motion. IS : 8686 - 1977 5.1.2.4 The test shall be carried out with allenergizing energizing quantities disconnected from the relay. 5.1.3 Criteria for Acceptance with all relevant per5.1.3.1 After the test the relay shall still comply formance requirements specified in IS : 3231-1965*. and auxiliary

NOTE - A flashover (capacitance discharge) is not necessarily a criteria of failure as this may occur in a position that does no damage and the manufacturer shall decide whether or not to eliminate the cause provided other criteria of acceptance are met.

5.1.3.2 The impulse test is designed as a type test and should not Since repeated stressing may normally be made on production relays. reduce the performance and/or life, any impulse tests which are carried out after the relaysleave the manufacturer's works should be limited to a maximum of 60 percent of the class voltage assigned by the manufacturer. 5.2 High Frequency Disturbance Test

5.2.1 High frequency disturbance test is recommended in order to determine whether a relay will operate in a faulty manner when specified high frequency transients which are representative of practical system conditions are applied to a fuNy energized relay.
NOTE - One frequency is considered to be justified as a test to be applied to all relays irrespective of design and gives a basic indication of the ability of the relay to withstand high frequency disturbances. Other test frequencies and other types of tests may be proved necessary in future and those will be added as experience develops.

5.2.2

Test Circuit Conditions Waveform -A damped oscillatory wave with the envelope decaying to 50 percent of peak value at the end of 3 to 6 cycles. 1 .O MHz with a tolerance 200 ohms with a tolerance of-!, of& 10 percent. 10 percent.
